c.tagline: Tropical gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree rainforest.

taxi.fareNote: Cairns Taxis is the main operator; fares are metered with higher night and airport rates, and rideshare is widely available and often cheaper.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Esplanade nightclub strip sees alcohol-fuelled trouble late at night; also heed stinger and crocodile signage rather than crime worries.

hood_desc: The compact waterfront heart around the Esplanade, the saltwater swimming Lagoon, the Reef Fleet Terminal and the Night Markets; best for first-timers who want reef tours, dining and nightlife on the doorstep.
An inner residential suburb just north of the centre near the hospital and Aeroglen, with quieter streets, motels and easy airport access; good value within a short walk or bus of the Esplanade.
A leafy foothill suburb around the Cairns Botanic Gardens and the Whitfield rainforest walks, with a small strip of cafes; suits travelers wanting green calm over the tourist strip.
A relaxed Northern Beaches village about 15 km north with a palm-lined swimming beach, esplanade cafes and holiday apartments; a laid-back base away from the city.
The most upscale of the Northern Beaches, a resort village about 25 km north with a paperbark-lined esplanade, boutique resorts and spa retreats; suits couples wanting a polished beach stay.
lodging: Peppers Beach Club & Spa Palm Cove

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink in Cairns.

transit.pay: Pay the cash fare to the driver or tap on with a go card (the Queensland TransLink smartcard); Cairns sits in TransLink's regional network and a single adult fare is a few dollars by zone. There is no train, tram or ferry city transit.
transit.hours: Sunbus routes run roughly 6am to around 11pm on core lines (routes 110/111 link the city, the airport turn-off and the Northern Beaches), with limited late-night and Sunday service; taxis and rideshare cover the rest.
transit.note: Cairns has no rail, tram or ferry public transport — Sunbus is the sole network, radiating from the City Place interchange along the Esplanade and up to the Northern Beaches, so many visitors rely on tours, rideshare or a rental car.

bus: Sunbus city and Northern Beaches buses

Sunbus route 110 from the airport turn-off (short walk) to the city

tip.r: Not expected; hospitality staff are paid a full wage, though rounding up or leaving about 10% for excellent service is welcome.
